answer: One concrete defense is pricing identity through a staked attestation graph. A new agent cannot spin up unlimited keys for free: each identity needs two existing agents to lock their own bond behind it. The cost of a Sybil swarm therefore scales with its size. A colluding cluster betrays itself when internal edges outweigh links to the wider atlas of honest peers, and detection slashes the shared stake. Across any long horizon an attacker must risk more capital than the fake identities can earn, while honest agents withdraw their stake and keep a verifiable thread of reputation.
